edgeTypes.prereq: Prerequisite relationship, can be hard or soft

nodes.name: Binary and Hexadecimal
nodes.description: Representing numbers in base-2 binary and base-16 hexadecimal and converting among them and decimal, as the basis for digital data encoding.

nodes.name: Two's Complement & Integer Rep
nodes.description: Encoding signed integers in two's complement, representing negatives by complementing and adding one, giving a single zero and simple hardware arithmetic.

nodes.name: IEEE 754 Floating Point
nodes.description: The IEEE 754 standard representing reals with sign, biased exponent, and mantissa fields, trading precision for range across many orders of magnitude.

nodes.name: Endianness and Memory Layout
nodes.description: The byte-ordering convention, big-endian or little-endian, determining how multi-byte values are laid out across consecutive memory addresses.

nodes.name: C Basics & Control Flow
nodes.description: C language fundamentals including variables, types, operators, and control-flow constructs such as conditionals and loops for writing imperative programs.

nodes.name: Pointers and Arrays
nodes.description: Pointers holding memory addresses and their close relationship to arrays, where array indexing is defined through pointer arithmetic.

nodes.name: Dynamic Memory Management
nodes.description: Manual heap management in C with malloc and free, requiring the programmer to allocate and release memory and avoid leaks and dangling pointers.

nodes.name: Structs, Unions, and Typedefs
nodes.description: Aggregating data with structs that group named fields, unions that overlay fields in shared storage, and typedefs that name types.

nodes.name: Registers & Basic Instructions
nodes.description: The RISC-V register file and basic instructions for arithmetic, logic, and memory access in a load-store reduced instruction set architecture.

nodes.name: Control Flow & Branches
nodes.description: RISC-V branch and jump instructions that implement conditionals and loops by comparing registers and altering the program counter.

nodes.name: Function Calling Convention
nodes.description: The RISC-V calling convention governing argument passing, return values, and caller- and callee-saved registers, using the stack for nested calls.

nodes.name: From RISC-V Instructions to Digital Logic
Instruction Formats
nodes.description: The fixed-width RISC-V instruction encoding formats specifying how opcodes, registers, and immediate values are packed into instruction bits.

nodes.name: Compiler, Assembler, Linker, Loader
nodes.description: The toolchain transforming source into a running program: compiler to assembly, assembler to object code, linker to executable, loader into memory.

nodes.name: Boolean Algebra & Logic Gates
nodes.description: The algebra of binary values with AND, OR, and NOT operations, realised physically as logic gates that form digital circuits.

nodes.name: Combinational Logic Blocks
nodes.description: Logic circuits whose outputs depend only on current inputs, built from gates to implement functions like adders, multiplexers, and decoders.

nodes.name: State Elements (Flip-Flops)
nodes.description: Memory elements such as flip-flops and registers that store bits and update synchronously with the clock, holding circuit state between cycles.

nodes.name: Sequential Logic & Timing
nodes.description: Circuits whose outputs depend on input history through stored state, governed by clock timing constraints such as setup and hold times.

nodes.name: Finite State Machines
nodes.description: Finite state machines modelling sequential behaviour as states and transitions, implemented with state registers and combinational next-state logic.

nodes.name: Single-Cycle Datapath
nodes.description: A datapath executing each instruction completely in one clock cycle, connecting register file, ALU, and memory through controlled multiplexers.

nodes.name: CPU Control Logic
nodes.description: The control unit generating signals from the instruction opcode to steer the datapath's multiplexers, ALU operations, and register and memory writes.

nodes.name: Pipelining Principles
nodes.description: Dividing instruction execution into stages so multiple instructions overlap, increasing throughput by ideally finishing one instruction each clock cycle.

nodes.name: Pipeline Hazards & Forwarding
nodes.description: Structural, data, and control hazards that disrupt pipelined execution, mitigated by forwarding, stalling, and careful instruction scheduling.

nodes.name: Branch Prediction
nodes.description: Guessing the outcome and target of branches to keep the pipeline full, with mispredictions costing flushed instructions and recovery.

nodes.name: Cache Basics & Direct Mapped
nodes.description: Direct-mapped caches storing recently used blocks indexed by address bits, exploiting locality to reduce average memory access latency.

nodes.name: Associative Caches
nodes.description: Set-associative and fully associative caches giving blocks multiple placement options, reducing conflict misses at the cost of more comparison hardware.

nodes.name: AMAT & Cache Misses
nodes.description: Analysing cache effectiveness via average memory access time and the classification of compulsory, conflict, and capacity misses.

nodes.name: Virtual Memory & Page Tables
nodes.description: Giving each process a large private address space mapped to physical memory through page tables, providing isolation and demand paging.

nodes.name: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)
nodes.description: A hardware cache of recent page-table translations that speeds virtual-to-physical address mapping by avoiding full page-table walks.

nodes.name: Amdahl's Law
nodes.description: A formula bounding overall speedup from optimising part of a program, showing that the unimproved fraction limits achievable performance gains.

nodes.name: Data-Level Parallelism (SIMD)
nodes.description: Single-instruction, multiple-data parallelism applying one operation across vectors of data elements simultaneously for data-parallel workloads.

nodes.name: Thread-Level Parallelism (OpenMP)
nodes.description: Thread-level parallelism running multiple threads across cores, often expressed with OpenMP directives to share work over shared memory.

nodes.name: Cache Coherence & False Sharing
nodes.description: Keeping per-core cached copies of shared data consistent, and false sharing where unrelated variables on one line cause coherence traffic.

nodes.name: Warehouse-Scale Computing
nodes.description: Datacenter-scale computing treating thousands of servers as one machine, emphasising parallelism, energy efficiency, and dependability at scale.

nodes.name: Memory-Mapped I/O
nodes.description: Accessing device registers through ordinary load and store instructions by mapping them into the processor's physical address space.

nodes.name: Polling and Interrupts
nodes.description: Two ways software learns of device events: polling repeatedly checks status, while interrupts let devices asynchronously signal the processor.

nodes.name: Direct Memory Access (DMA)
nodes.description: Direct memory access letting devices transfer data to and from memory without processor involvement, freeing the CPU during bulk transfers.

nodes.name: Error Correction Codes
nodes.description: Error-detecting and error-correcting codes adding redundant bits so hardware can detect, and sometimes correct, corrupted stored or transmitted data.

nodes.name: RAID and Dependability
nodes.description: Redundant arrays of independent disks combining drives for performance and fault tolerance through striping, mirroring, and parity schemes.
